title: Margin note: prompts that evolve in a market
body:
What the note says: LLM agents that differ only in their system prompts trade in a simulated market, and bankrupt agents are replaced by mutated copies of successful prompts. A market that rewards accuracy ends at 94% accuracy with high token use; a per-token cost market collapses accuracy to 10%, because token use and accuracy move together.

What would need to be true:
- Is the coupling a property of the models, or of how the prompts are mutated?
- Would the collapse to 10% survive a market that prices both accuracy and tokens?
- How many runs and model families? The note does not say.

From the collected note only. The paper is next on my list.
